newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutz sees 1996 group net above 800 mln marks.
newsitem.headline: Deutz sees 1996 group net above 800 mln marks.

text.p: German machinery maker Deutz AG said on Monday it expected to report a group net profit of over 800 million marks in 1996 compared to the 1.13 billion mark loss it made in 1995.

It also said that in the current year stronger revenues and volumes, together with the improved currency situation, growth opportunities in the U.S. and Asia as well as a better cost structure, "created the basis for significant profit increases compared to the previous year".
Deutz said the net profit will go towards compensating for the 1995 balance sheet loss of 951.9 million marks and to reinstate an equity capital of more than 200 million marks.
Deutz, formerly named Kloeckner-Humboldt-Deutz AG, was rescued last year in a one-billion mark bank bailout after discovering heavy losses relating to plant construction contracts in Saudi Arabia.
The company said the restructuring had reduced its net indebtedness to 602 million marks by the end of December 1996, marking a 61 percent fall in the last two years.
Group new orders in 1996 fell to 2.696 billion marks from 3.125 billion while sales fell to 2.922 billion marks from 3.285 billion, Deutz said.
